answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, please do not run every day. New-runner legs need the day off between runs to adapt, and skipping rest is the fastest way to a niggle that stops you altogether. Three run days plus your dog walks is plenty to be ready for Nov 15. We will get there by making each run a little longer and the walk breaks a little shorter, not by adding days.

new.analysis:
You did the hardest part: you started and you repeated it three times. Pain was 0/10, heart rate stayed controlled, and you finished Saturday feeling proud. That is exactly the launch pad we want for a 10-week build to the 5K.

The main lever for the next few weeks is time on feet, not speed. I am adding roughly a minute to each run and lengthening Saturday a touch, keeping your 1 min run and 1 min walk pattern. If Saturday feels easy, we will stretch the run intervals the week after.

Keep the dog walks on the in-between days, because easy walking helps recovery without adding strain. If your calves ever stay tight into the next afternoon, back off that day and tell me in your check-in.
